instructions: Answer any three out of the remaining five questions.
Assume any suitable data wherever required and justify the same.

questions.label: 1a
questions.text: Distinguish between Name node and Data node.

questions.label: 1b
questions.text: List and explain the core business drivers behind the NoSQL movement.

questions.label: 1c
questions.text: Mention four characteristics of big data. Elaborate these characteristics with respect to social media websites.

questions.label: 1d
questions.text: List and explain the different issues and challenges in data stream query processing.

questions.label: 2a
questions.text: What is a key-value store? What are the benefits of using a key-value store?

questions.label: 2b
questions.text:
Write a map reduce pseudo code to multiply two matrices. Apply map reduce working to perform following matrix multiplication.

$$
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \times \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 7 \\ 8 & 9 \end{bmatrix}
$$

questions.label: 3a
questions.text: Suppose the stream is S = \{2, 1, 6, 1, 5, 9, 2, 3, 5\}. Let hash functions h(x) = ax + b mod 16 for some a and b, treat result as a 4-bit binary integer. Show how the Flajolet-Martin algorithm will estimate the number of distinct elements, h(x) = 4x + 1 mod 16.

questions.label: 3b
questions.text:
Consider the following data frame given below:

| course | id | class | marks |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 11 | 1 | 56 |
| 2 | 12 | 2 | 75 |
| 3 | 13 | 1 | 48 |
| 4 | 14 | 2 | 69 |
| 5 | 15 | 1 | 84 |
| 6 | 16 | 2 | 53 |

i. Create a subset of course less than 3 by using [ ] brackets and demonstrate the output.

ii. Create a subset where the course column is less than 3 or the class equals to 2 by using subset () function and demonstrate the output.

questions.label: 4a
questions.text: Explain natural join and grouping and aggregation relational algebraic operation using MapReduce.

questions.label: 4b
questions.text: With a neat sketch, explain the architecture of the data-stream management system.

questions.label: 5a
questions.text: Determine communities for the given social network graph using Girvan-Newman algorithm.
questions.note: Graph in the paper, edges: A-B, A-C, B-C, C-D, D-E, D-F, E-F.

questions.label: 5b
questions.text: List and discuss various types of data structures in R.

questions.label: 6a
questions.text:
i. The following table shows the number of units of different products sold on different days:

| Product | Monday | Tuesday | Wednesday | Thursday | Friday |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bread | 12 | 3 | 5 | 11 | 9 |
| Milk | 21 | 27 | 18 | 20 | 15 |
| Cola Cans | 10 | 1 | 33 | 6 | 12 |
| Chocolate bars | 6 | 7 | 4 | 13 | 12 |
| Detergent | 5 | 8 | 12 | 20 | 23 |

Create five sample numeric vectors from this data.

ii. Name and explain the operators used to form data subsets in R.

questions.label: 6b
questions.text: Define collaborative filtering. Using an example of an e-commerce site like flipkart or amazon describe how it can be used to provide recommendation to users.
